battle.name: 尼泊爾內戰
battle.brief: 尼泊爾內戰於一九九六年在尼泊爾中西部山區爆發，起因包括地方治理、土地與政治不平等，毛主義游擊隊與政府及治安部隊的對抗並在鄉村形成長期游擊戰；鐵甲艦（Ironclad）是英國十九世紀蒸汽動力裝甲戰艦的正式型號，屬海上重型火力平台。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 鐵甲艦是英國皇家海軍十九世紀蒸汽動力艦隊中的裝甲戰艦類別，憑厚重船體與艦載火炮承擔海上火力骨幹。

countries: 本篇實錄以一九九六年一月至十二月為界，記錄「尼泊爾內戰」中王國政府與尼泊爾共產黨（毛主義）及其人民解放軍之間的衝突，而不是兩國交戰。政治與最高指揮中心在加德滿都，戰鬥沿普里特維公路、馬亨德拉公路及阿蘭尼科公路向兩側山地擴散；Baglung、Palpa、Syangja與Myagdi等西部山區，以及Rautahat、Udayapur與Sindhuli等中東部丘陵，成為游擊、設阻與清剿反覆轉換的地帶。印度是政府軍火供應、訓練和外交協調的重要外部因素，中國北方邊境亦有跨境流動與查緝，但一九九六年沒有外國正規部隊加入任何一方作戰。
countriesEn: This record covers January through December 1996 and follows the conflict inside the Kingdom of Nepal between the royal government, the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist), and its People's Liberation Army; it was not a war between two states. The political and supreme command center was Kathmandu, while fighting spread from the Prithvi, Mahendra, and Araniko highways into the hills on both sides. Baglung, Palpa, Syangja, and Myagdi in the western hills, together with Rautahat, Udayapur, and Sindhuli in the central and eastern hills, repeatedly changed hands between guerrilla action, obstruction, and clearing operations. India was an important external factor in government arms supply, training, and diplomatic coordination. Cross-border movement and enforcement also existed along China's northern frontier, but no foreign regular force fought for either side in 1996.
people: 一九九六年二月，王國政府由Birendra主持政治轉折，二月十七日任命Sher Bahadur Deuba為首相；十月九日公布的憲法修正繼續採行首相與內閣制。軍隊最高層是陸軍參謀長Gopal Gurung，警察總監K.P. Nepal負責警察與內部秩序，野戰單位由Army師、旅、營及警察武裝單位分開指揮，後勤則維持專責體系。CPN(M)方面，Prachanda任總書記並掌握PLA最高戰術權，PLA依中央委員會、數字師、營級突擊隊及縣級游擊支隊分層，突擊群通常由基層指揮官帶領小分隊進入目標區，行動後即分散重組。這種結構使雙方指揮方式一端依賴固定營區與交通線，另一端依賴分散、臨時編成的突擊群，兩套體系很難在同一時間對同一戰場集中火力。
peopleEn: On the government side, King Birendra presided over the political transition in February, and Sher Bahadur Deuba was appointed prime minister on 17 February; a constitutional amendment promulgated on 9 October continued the prime-ministerial and cabinet system. The highest military echelon was Army Chief of Staff Gopal Gurung, while Inspector General of Police K.P. Nepal handled policing and internal security. Field units were separately commanded through Army divisions, brigades, and battalions, together with Armed Police units and a dedicated logistics system. For the CPN(M), Prachanda served as general secretary and held the PLA's highest tactical authority. The PLA was layered from the Central Committee through numbered divisions, battalion strike teams, and district guerrilla detachments; strike-group commanders normally led small detachments into the target area and dispersed to regroup after an action. One command system therefore depended on fixed garrisons and transport routes, while the other relied on dispersed, temporarily formed strike groups, making it difficult for either to concentrate fire on the same battlefield at the same time.
kits: 政府武裝的制式步槍包括5.56×45公厘INSAS、7.62×39公厘SKS、7.62×51公厘FN FAL與印度式SLR，近戰使用9×19公厘Sterling；FN MAG 7.62×51公厘通用機槍、L16 81公厘迫擊砲及RPG-7 40公厘火箭筒提供火力。車輛有Land Rover 110與軍用卡車，後勤沿公路把不同口徑的彈藥分送至加德滿都、博卡拉及前線區，再由作戰人員和軍馬分段背負。PLA在山地分隊可見的口徑更雜，常以繳獲的.303 Lee-Enfield、7.62×51 SLR或FAL、9×19 Sterling為主，亦有RPG-7及Mills手榴彈；其彈藥依突擊所得數量摻用，沒有政府軍完整的備份。INSAS常用三十發匣，FAL用二十發匣，SLR與SKS則是十發內倉，因此混合裝備的分隊必須分別攜帶不同彈匣與備彈。
kitsEn: Standard rifles of the government armed forces included the 5.56×45mm INSAS, 7.62×39mm SKS, 7.62×51mm FN FAL, and Indian-pattern SLR, while the 9×19mm Sterling was used for close-range fighting. Support fire came from the FN MAG 7.62×51mm general-purpose machine gun, the L16 81mm mortar, and the RPG-7 40mm rocket launcher. Vehicles included Land Rover 110s and military trucks, while logistics moved ammunition of different calibers by road to Kathmandu, Pokhara, and forward areas before combat personnel and pack animals carried it in stages. PLA mountain detachments operated a more varied mix, commonly using captured .303 Lee-Enfield, 7.62×51 SLR or FAL, and 9×19 Sterling, together with RPG-7s and Mills grenades. Their ammunition was mixed according to what had been taken from opposing stocks, without the complete reserve system maintained by the government. The INSAS commonly used thirty-round magazines, the FAL twenty-round magazines, and the SLR and SKS ten-round internal magazines, so detachments using mixed weapons had to carry separate magazines and ammunition.
tactics: 一九九六年的戰術主線，是從都會區的分散襲擊轉向山區的持久游擊。二月攻擊中，PLA以數個小隊分別攻擊巡邏隊、崗哨與警察總部，多點同時發生，使政府指揮系統必須同時處理多個警情；進入山區後，突擊隊沿林緣、嶺脊和峽谷接近孤立警站，先切斷道路與電話，再集中攻擊駐軍，得手後不維持正面陣地，而沿支稜撤離並重組。政府軍則由警察守住城鎮、交通線與縣治所，陸軍營以公路為軸建立機動群，先封鎖進出道路，再以步兵分隊搜索山脊；迫擊砲則用於方位能由觀察哨確認的陣地。PLA避免與成建制的步兵營正面對峙，政府軍雖有較強火力，卻受制於道路、補給與白晝搜索條件，雙方因此形成截然不同的風險計算。
tacticsEn: The central tactical development of 1996 was a shift from dispersed attacks in the capital to sustained guerrilla warfare in the hills. During the February attacks, separate PLA teams struck patrols, checkpoints, and police headquarters, creating simultaneous incidents that forced the government command system to handle several emergencies at once. After entering the hills, strike teams approached isolated police stations along forest edges, ridgelines, and gullies, cut roads and telephone links, and then concentrated their attack on the garrison. Rather than maintain a frontal position, they withdrew along secondary ridges and regrouped. The government assigned police to hold towns, transport lines, and district seats, while Army companies built mobile groups around the roads, blocked routes in and out, and searched ridges with infantry detachments. Mortars were used against positions whose bearing could be confirmed by observation posts. The PLA avoided frontal engagements with formed infantry companies, while government firepower remained constrained by roads, supply, and the limits of daytime searching, giving the two sides sharply different calculations of risk.
data: 時間線始於一月國會重新運作及王室準備恢復多黨政治，二月十七日Deuba組閣；二月十八日，PLA在加德滿都及周邊同步攻擊警察目標，造成政府當時公布的十六名警員死亡，這是該次行動的官方傷亡數字，未用於延伸推算全年總量。二月下旬，加德滿都警察總部再遭爆炸攻擊，破壞建築並造成警員死亡，但完整逐人名單並不完整，因此不列推測數字。三月二日，政府與CPN(M)原則同意會談並暫停主要攻擊，數日內互信即因後續拘押及零星襲擊而削弱。四月談判正式破裂，四月底至五月，PLA把襲擊能力轉向中西部山區的基層警站，政府則投入Army師級部隊，部隊由加德滿都沿普里特維公路向博卡拉推進，再分向Baglung、Syangja、Palpa與Myagdi；警察退守城鎮及縣治所，Army以小型清剿隊逐個奪回失守警站。五月至九月雨季，公路泥濘、通信中斷與搜索隊疲勞降低政府推進速度，PLA趁隙攻擊外圍警站，取得武器彈藥後退回山地。十月九日憲法修正公布；十一月政府與PLA代表在Pokhara會談，未形成有約束力的停火協議。十二月底，雙方仍分別控制主要城市、公路與一批山地陣地，談判管道未完全中斷，但軍事衝突沒有停止。
dataEn: The chronology began in January with the parliament resuming work and the monarchy preparing to restore multiparty politics. Deuba formed his cabinet on 17 February. On 18 February, the PLA launched synchronized attacks against police targets in and around Kathmandu, causing sixteen police personnel to be killed according to the government's published toll for the action; this official figure was not used to extrapolate a total for the year. In late February, a further explosion struck Kathmandu police headquarters, damaging the building and killing police personnel, but no complete individual list was available, so no inferred figure is given. On 2 March, the government and the CPN(M) agreed in principle to talks and a pause in major attacks, although trust weakened within days because of subsequent arrests and isolated attacks. The talks broke down formally in April. From late April through May, the PLA redirected its attack capability toward基层 police stations in the central and western hills. The government committed divisional Army units, moving from Kathmandu along the Prithvi Highway to Pokhara and then branching toward Baglung, Syangja, Palpa, and Myagdi. Police withdrew to towns and district seats while Army clearing detachments retaken lost stations one by one. From May through September, muddy roads, broken communications, and fatigue slowed government advances during the monsoon, allowing the PLA to strike outer stations, take weapons and ammunition, and return to the hills. The constitutional amendment was promulgated on 9 October. In November, government and PLA representatives held talks in Pokhara without reaching a binding ceasefire agreement. By the end of December, each side still held major towns, roads, and a number of mountain positions; the contact channel had not completely collapsed, but military conflict continued.
cause: 一九九六年的升級並非由單一事件造成。一九九○年的民主運動迫使王權退讓，一九九一年選舉與議會恢復後，國王仍對軍隊及警察高層的任命保有重大影響，CPN(M)未加入政府，繼續要求以制憲方式解決王權問題；該黨在一九九三年遭禁止與逮捕後，核心幹部及武裝人員轉入地下。到一九九六年，王室重新開放憲政途徑，並安排次年五月選舉，CPN(M)認為此舉將使現有軍警架構取得新的合法性，於是加強游擊部署。三月至四月的談判又因目的、核查方式及停火次序沒有共識而破裂，使雙方回到武力解決的選項。地形則把這種升級變得可行：山區道路少、季風限制搜索，PLA可以保存並分散兵力，政府軍雖有較強火力，卻難以把戰力投送到每個前線據點。
causeEn: The escalation of 1996 did not result from a single event. The democracy movement of 1990 forced the monarchy to retreat, and after elections and the restoration of parliament in 1991, the king still exercised substantial influence over senior army and police appointments. The CPN(M) did not join the government and continued to seek a constituent solution to the monarchy. After the party was banned and its leaders arrested in 1993, its central cadres and armed personnel went underground. By 1996, the monarchy had reopened the constitutional route and arranged elections for May of the following year. The CPN(M) concluded that this process would grant legitimacy to the existing military and police structure, so it expanded its guerrilla deployments. Talks from March to April then collapsed because there was no agreement on their purpose, verification arrangements, or ceasefire sequence, returning both sides to military options. Terrain made the escalation practicable: mountain roads were scarce, the monsoon restricted searching, and the PLA could preserve and disperse its forces, while the government had stronger firepower but could not deliver it to every forward position.
impact: 到一九九六年底，衝突的形態已由零星襲擊轉為較持久的山區戰爭。PLA建立了數字師與突擊分隊的作戰架構，取得武器後補充火力，並在山地維持較固定的後勤基地；政府則把警察由前線攻擊者主要改為據點守備力量，由Army營輪流投入搜索與奪回警站。地理控制也呈現混合狀態：政府仍保有加德滿都、主要公路、若干縣治所與較強常備火力，但外圍陣地屢易手，PLA則能在受干擾的山區重新集結。首都攻擊沒有推翻十月完成的憲政程序，反而促使政府同時維持鎮壓與談判兩種手段，並從印度取得更多軍火及訓練支援。雙方發布的戰鬥傷亡數字口徑不同，許多前線事件缺乏可核實名冊，因此不能建立可信的全年總表。
impactEn: By the end of 1996, the conflict had changed from isolated attacks into a more sustained mountain war. The PLA had established a structure of numbered divisions and strike detachments, replenished firepower with captured weapons, and maintained relatively fixed logistics bases in the hills. The government shifted police from serving mainly as attackers to holding fortified posts, while Army companies rotated through searching for and retaking stations. Geographic control was mixed: the government retained Kathmandu, the principal highways, several district seats, and a stronger standing firepower base, but outer positions changed hands repeatedly, and the PLA could reassemble in disrupted mountain areas. The capital attacks did not overturn the constitutional process completed in October. Instead, the government maintained both military pressure and negotiations, while receiving additional arms and training support from India. The two sides published battle-loss figures on incompatible bases, and many forward incidents lacked verifiable personnel lists, preventing the construction of a credible annual total.
result: 一九九六年的結果不是一場決定性的戰場勝負。PLA未能在年內攻入加德滿都或摧毀政府中樞；政府也未能消滅PLA、永久固定所有曾失守的警站，或迫使對方無條件解除武裝。PLA保有山地游擊主力並靠繳獲擴充火力，政府仍控制加德滿都、主要公路、若干縣治所與較強的常備火力，但不少外圍陣地需要反覆爭奪。十一月Pokhara會談沒有達成有約束力協議，短暫停火也未形成持續安排，因此年尾的實際狀態是談判未斷、戰鬥未停。這一年度的內戰至此由加德滿都周邊的襲擊與零星突擊，轉為以山區據點、道路封鎖和季節性進攻為核心的長期消耗；衝突隨後延續至一九九七年及以後。
resultEn: The result of 1996 was not a decisive battlefield victory. The PLA neither entered Kathmandu nor destroyed the government's command center during the year. The government could not eliminate the PLA, permanently secure every station that had fallen, or compel its opponent to disarm unconditionally. The PLA retained its mountain guerrilla force and expanded its firepower with captured weapons. The government continued to hold Kathmandu, the principal highways, several district seats, and a stronger standing firepower base, although many outer positions still had to be contested repeatedly. The November talks in Pokhara produced no binding agreement, and the temporary ceasefires did not become a sustained arrangement. The practical condition at the year's end was therefore that negotiations remained open while fighting continued. The 1996 civil-war record thus ended with attacks and raids around Kathmandu giving way to a prolonged contest based on mountain positions, road blocks, and seasonal offensives, a conflict that continued into 1997 and afterward.
